assessment.nobel_worthiness: The misallocation framework gave a powerful, portable account of productivity and income differences, joining firm-level distortions to aggregate development outcomes.
assessment.attribution: The three credited researchers form a coherent attribution for the quantitative measurement and theory of allocative inefficiency across firms.
assessment.maturity: The approach has been extensively used, tested, extended and debated across growth, development and macroeconomics.
uncertainties: Measured wedges can reflect factors other than policy-relevant misallocation, complicating causal interpretation.
The broad literature makes sharp delimitation of the prize-recognized contribution important.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Firm heterogeneity and selection transformed modern trade analysis and clarified how trade reallocates activity, productivity and welfare.
assessment.attribution: Melitz is central to the canonical heterogeneous-firm model, while Helpman and Redding represent major theoretical development and dissemination of this research program.
assessment.maturity: The framework is foundational in contemporary trade and has generated a substantial empirical and quantitative literature.
uncertainties: Credit for the wider heterogeneous-firm trade literature extends beyond any three-person allocation.
The size and distribution of gains remain sensitive to model assumptions and data.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Dynamic-panel GMM methods supplied indispensable tools for identifying dynamic relationships with individual effects and endogenous regressors.
assessment.attribution: Arellano, Blundell and Bond have clear and closely connected claims to the landmark estimators and their practical implementation.
assessment.maturity: The methods are long established, widely taught and central to empirical work in many fields.
uncertainties: Weak-instrument and finite-sample problems require careful use and qualify some applied conclusions.
The contribution is methodological, so its broad scientific impact must be weighed against more substantive discoveries.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: This work reshaped understanding of how technology, tasks and trade shocks affect local labour markets, employment and inequality.
assessment.attribution: Autor, Dorn and Hanson constitute a well-defined core for the empirical task and trade-shock research program.
assessment.maturity: Its evidence and methods have influenced labour economics, trade, political economy and policy discussion for many years.
uncertainties: Separating technological change, globalization and other local shocks remains empirically difficult.
The appropriate division of credit between task-based theory and trade-shock evidence is contestable.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Collateral constraints and financial amplification became core mechanisms for analyzing credit cycles and macroeconomic fluctuations.
assessment.attribution: Kiyotaki and Moore provide the seminal collateral-cycle mechanism, with Gertler central to the financial-accelerator formulation.
assessment.maturity: The mechanisms are deeply incorporated in modern macro-finance models and gained added salience after financial crises.
uncertainties: Several adjacent macro-finance traditions make the boundaries of the contribution difficult to draw.
Quantitative importance of the mechanisms varies across episodes and models.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The research established management practices and organizational capital as measurable, consequential determinants of firm productivity and development.
assessment.attribution: Bloom and Van Reenen are central to the original measurement agenda, and Sadun is a major contributor to its organizational and applied development.
assessment.maturity: The evidence has accumulated across countries, sectors and experimental or quasi-experimental designs.
uncertainties: Management measures can be endogenous to unobserved firm capabilities.
The relative roles of individual scholars and collaborators across the broad program require careful attribution.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Heterogeneous-agent New Keynesian models materially advanced analysis of fiscal and monetary transmission through households' balance sheets and marginal propensities to consume.
assessment.attribution: Kaplan, Moll and Violante form a natural core for the influential quantitative framework.
assessment.maturity: The framework is now highly influential in policy-oriented macroeconomics, though comparatively recent.
uncertainties: Its empirical discipline and policy conclusions remain sensitive to household heterogeneity, expectations and market-incompleteness assumptions.
The contribution may need more time to demonstrate durable influence relative to older macroeconomic frameworks.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Their long-run datasets and comparative analysis made sovereign debt, banking crises and default central to empirical international macroeconomics.
assessment.attribution: Reinhart and Rogoff are plainly identified with the integrated historical crisis research program.
assessment.maturity: The work has had enduring scholarly and policy influence and stimulated extensive follow-on research.
uncertainties: Some prominent empirical claims and data practices have received substantial criticism and reanalysis.
Historical regularities do not by themselves establish invariant causal mechanisms.
